en: Clearly, AI agents are useful, but not every
tool that uses AI is necessarily an AI
agent, and not every task requires an AI
agent. You can also have workflows that may
be powered by AI. Now,
what's the difference though? The difference
is that the AI agent is powered by that
agent loop where the model makes decisions
and the harness then executes them and runs
those tools. And we have that cycle that
keeps on going until a goal is reached. So
the model drives and makes the decisions. A
workflow, on the other hand, is a predefined
deterministic sequence of steps that are
always the same. There is no randomness in
there. There are no decisions made by a
model in there. That's the key difference.
For example, if you want to handle incoming
emails by customers, let's say,
you may want to summarize them. You may
wanna classify them. Maybe you also wanna
store them in a database and not use AI at
all for that task.
That's a perfect example for a workflow. You
know that for a given input, an email
arriving at a certain address, you wanna
execute a certain step. Let's say summarize
it. And then you know that you will have a
summary and in some follow-up step, you may
save that in a database, whatever. You may
have more steps.
But it's a clearly defined workflow. You
don't want an AI model here making decisions
because it could make the wrong decisions.
You don't want randomness. You want a
predictable flow of steps. And it turns out
that quite a lot of problems actually want
such a predictable flow of steps.
Just as AI agents can be very useful for
certain tasks,
for example, for general work where you have
all kinds of tasks in your day-to-day work
and therefore you need flexibility,
or with our customer support agent, where we
have all kinds of customer-related
questions. So where you need some
flexibility in some cases,
you also have other cases where you don't
want flexibility, but where you instead want
predictability and you want to have a clear
sequence of steps. That's why in this
course, we'll also explore how such a
workflow could be built and would look like
under the hood.
